plain: Generate a modern Ed25519 SSH key pair — a private key on your machine and a public key you can share.
when: You're setting up SSH or GitHub access and want key-based login instead of a password.

flags.meaning: key type (ed25519 is the modern default)

plain: Generate 32 random bytes and print them as 64 hex characters — a strong secret for tokens or keys.
when: You need a random API key, session secret, or password salt and don't want to invent one.

plain: Print the SHA-256 fingerprint of a file so you can compare it with the published checksum.
when: You downloaded an installer or release and want to verify it wasn't corrupted or tampered with.

flags.meaning: check files against a checksum list

plain: Probe a host and try to identify the service and version running on each open port.
when: You're mapping a machine you own or have written permission to test. Never scan networks that aren't yours.

flags.meaning: skip host discovery, assume it's up

plain: Open TCP port 22 in the Ubuntu firewall so SSH connections are allowed.
when: You enabled ufw and locked yourself out of SSH — allow the port before enabling the firewall.

plain: Fetch only the HTTP response headers, without downloading the page body.
when: You want to check status codes, redirects, caching, or security headers quickly.

flags.meaning: send a HEAD request and show headers only

plain: Decode a base64 file back into its original bytes.
when: You found a blob of base64 in a log, email, or CTF challenge and need the real content.

plain: Ask DNS for a domain's records and print only the answers.
when: You need to see what IP a domain resolves to, without dig's full output.

plain: Open a TLS connection and print the certificate chain and handshake details.
when: A site's HTTPS is failing, or you need to check certificate expiry and SNI behaviour.

plain: Scan the current folder for lines that look like hardcoded API keys, secrets, or tokens.
when: Right before pushing a repo public. Catches the classic 'oops, my key is in the code' mistake.
